Effective July 1, 2025, the State of Florida enacted SB 1768, which authorizes licensed physicians to administer certain stem cell therapies that have not been approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (“FDA”) for use in the treatment of orthopedic conditions, wound care and pain management, provided specified statutory requirements are met. Among other requirements, the Florida law establishes standards relating to the sourcing and manufacture of stem cell products, requires specified patient informed consent and disclosures that the therapies have not been approved by the FDA, and prohibits the use of stem cells derived from aborted fetuses or embryos.

Since Florida’s enactment of SB 1768, additional states have enacted legislation expanding access to certain stem cell and regenerative medicine therapies that have not been approved by the FDA. In 2026, Tennessee enacted HB 2246/SB 2586, Public Chapter 1016, which authorizes physicians to perform certain non-FDA-approved stem cell or regenerative medicine therapies when the treatment or procedure is within the physician’s scope of practice, subject to specified requirements. The principal operative provisions of the Tennessee law became effective July 1, 2026. Georgia also enacted HB 1275, Act 453, establishing requirements for the use of certain human stem cell therapies that have not been approved by the FDA, effective July 1, 2026. SB 1768, HB 2246/SB 2586, Public Chapter 1016 and HB 1275, Act 453 are sometimes referred to herein collectively, as the “New Stem Cell Laws.”

Other states, including Texas, Mississippi, North Carolina, Nevada and Utah, have enacted laws addressing or expanding patient access to certain stem cell or regenerative medicine therapies. The scope and requirements of these state laws vary, and additional states may enact similar legislation in the future.

The Company believes the enactment of these laws represents an emerging state-level regulatory framework that could expand physician and patient access to regenerative medicine therapies. Although the Company’s initial commercialization efforts have focused principally on Florida following the enactment of SB 1768, the enactment of legislation in Tennessee and Georgia provides the Company with additional potential markets in which it may seek to commercialize qualifying products, subject to the requirements of the applicable state laws and federal laws and regulations.

The Company believes that the expansion of state laws permitting access to certain non-FDA-approved stem cell and regenerative medicine therapies could increase demand from (i) patients who have historically traveled outside the United States to obtain certain regenerative medicine treatments, (ii) physicians and patients seeking access to regenerative medicine therapies not otherwise generally available under traditional treatment pathways, and (iii) physicians and healthcare practices seeking to incorporate regenerative medicine therapies into their practices.

By enabling physicians to adopt Zeo’s products for approved indications, the Company anticipates significant revenue growth and faster advancement of its clinical trial objectives at reduced cost. ZEO expects to further distinguish itself through leadership in research, quality, safety, and regulatory compliance for biologics. The new laws also allow Zeo to collect real-world safety and outcome data from providers—data that previously could only be obtained through FDA Investigational New Drug (IND) applications or Institutional Review Board (IRB)-approved studies. Access to this data is expected to lower risks associated with the Company’s future FDA submissions for product approvals.

While prioritizing the anticipated growth of the stem cell market in the United States, ZEO continues to advance its research programs, including clinical studies, product development, and ongoing quality and compliance initiatives. The Company recently launched two IRB-approved clinical studies titled “Open-Label Prospective Longitudinal Clinical Trial to Evaluate the Safety and Potential Efficacy of PPX™ in Patients Suffering from Musculoskeletal Joint Pathologies Using Real-World Data to Monitor Patient Outcomes” and “Open-Label Prospective Clinical Trial to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of Intracavernosal Plasma Precipitate Fraction (PPX) Plus Shockwave Therapy Versus Shockwave Therapy Alone in Adults with Erectile Dysfunction Using Real World Data to Monitor Patient Outcomes”. These studies have already begun enrollment and are expected to enroll up to 350 patients and 200 patients, respectively.

This shift is further supported by significant demographic trends, including an aging global population and increasing life expectancy. According to the U.S. Census Bureau, approximately 61.2 million Americans were aged 65 or older in 2024, representing approximately 18% of the U.S. population, with that number projected by the Population Reference Bureau to reach approximately 82 million by 2050. Similar demographic trends are occurring worldwide, creating increasing demand for innovative healthcare solutions addressing age-related conditions and quality of life. North America continues to represent the largest regional market with the United States representing a significant portion of this activity.

These demographic and market trends, coupled with continued scientific advances, increasing investment in biotechnology, and evolving state regulatory frameworks, including Florida’s 2025 legislation and Tennessee’s and Georgia’s 2026 legislation addressing certain stem cell therapies, may create substantial long-term opportunities for companies operating in the regenerative medicine sector. Other states, including Texas, Mississippi, North Carolina, Nevada, and Utah, have also adopted legislation addressing access to certain stem cell or regenerative medicine therapies, although the scope and requirements of these laws vary.

The Company believes these developments reflect growing recognition of the potential of regenerative medicine and represent an emerging commercial opportunity for qualified manufacturers and healthcare providers. The Company recognizes that the development, ownership, protection, and commercialization of intellectual property are integral to its long-term growth strategy and competitive positioning within the regenerative medicine and biotechnology industries. The Company’s intellectual property strategy encompasses three principal categories: (i) Company-developed intellectual property, including proprietary technologies, inventions, discoveries, manufacturing processes, methodologies, and other innovations developed internally through its research, development, and operational activities; (ii) licensed intellectual property, consisting of technologies, patents, proprietary processes, and other intellectual property developed by third parties for which the Company may acquire commercial rights through licensing agreements, acquisitions, or strategic partnerships; and (iii) jointly developed intellectual property, arising from research collaborations, joint development arrangements, and strategic relationships with scientists, academic institutions, research organizations, and commercial partners, with ownership and commercialization rights established through applicable contractual agreements.

Pursuant to agreements with its employees and consultants, the Company maintains contractual provisions designed to secure ownership of intellectual property and proprietary work product developed in connection with employment or work performed as a consultant relating to the Company’s existing or contemplated business activities, including applicable rights to patents, copyrights, trade secrets, and other intellectual property, subject to contractual exceptions and applicable law. Certain agreements also provide for the Company’s use of pre-existing intellectual property incorporated into Company-developed technologies through specified licensing arrangements. The Company believes that its ability to develop, acquire, protect, and commercialize intellectual property across these three categories provides an important foundation for innovation, strategic collaborations, potential licensing revenues, and long-term enterprise value creation. As the Company continues to expand its research and development initiatives, advanced cellular and extracellular vesicle technologies, and strategic relationships, it intends to pursue appropriate intellectual property protection measures, including patent applications, confidentiality agreements, invention assignments, licensing arrangements, and other contractual safeguards. The Company’s ability to obtain, maintain, enforce, and commercialize intellectual property rights remains subject to applicable laws, contractual limitations, regulatory requirements, and the inherent risks associated with developing emerging biotechnology products.

The regenerative medicine, biologics, and aesthetics industries in which the Company operates are dynamic, rapidly evolving, and characterized by continued scientific innovation, technological advancements, expanding market opportunities, and evolving regulatory frameworks. The Company competes with businesses engaged in the development, manufacturing, distribution, and commercialization of regenerative medicine products, cellular and tissue-based technologies, biologics, wound care solutions, and aesthetic products, as well as providers of conventional medical treatments and alternative therapeutic approaches. The Company believes that its integrated operating platform, advanced manufacturing infrastructure, specialized scientific capabilities, strategic location within a major research university, established physician relationships, commitment to quality assurance, and emphasis on professional education provide meaningful competitive strengths in this evolving marketplace. Principal competitive factors include product quality and consistency, safety, clinical evidence, manufacturing capabilities, regulatory compliance, physician acceptance, pricing, product availability, distribution efficiency, intellectual property, and the ability to provide comprehensive scientific, technical, and educational support to healthcare professionals.

A cornerstone of the Company’s competitive positioning is its biotechnology and manufacturing facility located on the campus of Nova Southeastern University (“NSU”), Florida’s largest private research university and an institution holding the “Carnegie R1” designation, the highest classification for research activity. The Company’s facility is situated within NSU’s approximately $100 million Center for Collaborative Research, a sophisticated research environment designed to support scientific discovery, technological innovation, and interdisciplinary collaboration. The Company’s dedicated facility incorporates ISO Class 7 cleanroom capabilities, specialized laboratory infrastructure, and manufacturing operations supported by established quality management systems and processes designed to meet applicable current Good Manufacturing Practice (“cGMP”) standards. The Company maintains an FDA-registered establishment and possesses specialized capabilities in cellular processing, extracellular vesicle characterization and analysis, microbiological testing, sterility assessment, and other analytical and quality-control procedures.

In addition to its own substantial investment in manufacturing and laboratory infrastructure, the Company benefits from access to NSU’s extensive array of sophisticated scientific instrumentation, specialized laboratory equipment, and advanced research resources. This access enables the Company to leverage capabilities beyond those maintained within its own facilities, potentially reducing the need for duplicative capital expenditures while supporting advanced analytical testing, research initiatives, product development, and scientific collaboration. Management further believes that the Company’s physical presence within a nationally recognized R1 research university represents a competitive advantage independent of its access to laboratory equipment and research infrastructure. Operating within this academic research environment provides opportunities to engage with scientific expertise, foster interdisciplinary collaborations, attract specialized scientific talent, and pursue relationships with researchers, clinicians, and academic institutions. The Company believes that the combination of its dedicated manufacturing infrastructure, access to NSU’s broader scientific resources, and strategic location within a major research university provides a distinctive competitive position that may be difficult for certain competitors to replicate. Management believes these advantages support the Company’s ability to pursue innovative regenerative medicine technologies, expand its scientific capabilities, and develop strategic relationships that may contribute to long-term commercial growth.

The Company also considers its regulatory history and commitment to quality assurance to be important elements of its competitive positioning. Since its inception, the Company has not received an FDA Warning Letter, a distinction management considers noteworthy within an industry that has experienced FDA scrutiny and enforcement activity involving certain stem cell, human cellular and tissue-based, and extracellular vesicle products. The Company believes that its investment in quality management systems, standardized manufacturing procedures, specialized laboratory testing, and ongoing regulatory compliance initiatives strengthens its ability to establish and maintain relationships with physicians, healthcare institutions, distributors, and strategic partners. Management views its regulatory history and operational discipline as important components of the Company’s commitment to product quality and long-term commercial development. The absence of an FDA Warning Letter, however, does not constitute FDA approval or a determination of regulatory compliance by the FDA and does not preclude future regulatory inquiries, inspections, or enforcement actions.

The Company believes that the healthcare industry’s increasing emphasis on preventive medicine, personalized healthcare, healthy aging, wellness, and longevity, together with continued advances in cellular and extracellular vesicle technologies, may contribute to growing demand for innovative regenerative medicine products and services. This broader evolution toward more personalized and proactive approaches to healthcare presents potential opportunities for companies engaged in developing and manufacturing advanced biological technologies. While third-party reimbursement remains an important consideration in the healthcare industry, many regenerative medicine therapies are currently offered through a cash-pay model. The Company’s near-term commercialization strategy for certain qualifying products is principally focused on the private-pay healthcare market, providing opportunities to establish direct relationships with physicians and healthcare practices without depending upon third-party reimbursement as a prerequisite for commercialization. The Company believes that increasing physician and patient awareness, expanding scientific research, and the development of additional clinical evidence may support broader market acceptance over time. Such evidence may be generated through FDA-authorized clinical trials, permitted research activities, and, where appropriate, the collection of real-world safety and patient outcome data, subject to applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

Management believes that the combination of the Company’s established operational infrastructure, regulatory history, specialized scientific capabilities, location within NSU’s R1 research environment, expanding commercial relationships, and commitment to innovation positions the Company to compete effectively and pursue opportunities for sustainable revenue growth and long-term shareholder value creation. Federal Regulatory Environment and Competition

The regulatory framework governing human cells, tissues, and cellular and tissue-based products (“HCT/Ps”) plays an important role in shaping the regenerative medicine industry, influencing product development, manufacturing standards, commercialization strategies, and competitive opportunities. The Company believes that the continued evolution of federal regulatory requirements, together with increasing scientific understanding of regenerative medicine technologies, may contribute to the development of a more clearly defined and sustainable marketplace. Management believes that companies possessing established manufacturing infrastructure, specialized scientific capabilities, comprehensive quality management systems, and the resources necessary to adapt to evolving regulatory requirements may be better positioned to compete as the industry continues to mature.

The FDA regulates HCT/Ps under a framework that distinguishes products eligible for regulation solely under Section 361 of the Public Health Service Act and 21 C.F.R. Part 1271 from products subject to additional regulation as drugs, devices, and/or biological products. The applicable regulatory pathway depends on several factors, including a product’s composition, degree of processing, intended use, and other relevant characteristics. Products requiring additional regulatory authorization may be subject to investigational new drug application (“IND”) requirements for clinical investigation and FDA approval or licensure, including through a biologics license application (“BLA”), before commercial marketing. Following the conclusion of the FDA’s enforcement discretion period for certain regenerative medicine products in May 2021, regulatory classification and compliance have remained important considerations for manufacturers and distributors operating within this industry.

The Company views its investment in advanced manufacturing capabilities, specialized laboratory infrastructure, quality assurance systems, and scientific expertise as important components of its strategy for operating within this evolving regulatory environment. The Company’s biotechnology and manufacturing facility at Nova Southeastern University’s Center for Collaborative Research, together with its ISO Class 7 cleanroom capabilities, analytical testing resources, and established quality management procedures, provides an operational foundation for pursuing product development, manufacturing, and commercialization opportunities under applicable regulatory frameworks. Management believes that these capabilities may enhance the Company’s ability to evaluate new technologies, support scientific research, maintain product quality and consistency, and adapt its operations as regulatory requirements and commercial opportunities evolve.

The Company has also sought guidance from experienced FDA regulatory counsel regarding its operations and the applicability of federal and state regulatory requirements to certain of its products and commercial activities. In particular, the Company has obtained a written legal opinion addressing its operations under Florida’s regulatory framework governing certain qualifying stem cell therapies. Management believes that this legal analysis, together with its ongoing compliance initiatives, supports the Company’s approach to pursuing opportunities under applicable state laws. Such legal opinions do not constitute FDA approval, authorization, or a binding determination by federal regulatory authorities, and the Company recognizes that state legislation does not supersede applicable federal requirements. The Company has not obtained an FDA ruling or determination confirming the regulatory classification or compliance status of all products it manufactures or distributes. Accordingly, although the Company believes it has identified regulatory basis for its current activities, there can be no assurance that the FDA will agree with its interpretations or will not determine that one or more products require additional authorization.

The Company believes that the increasing emphasis on scientific validation, product quality, regulatory compliance, and manufacturing consistency may create opportunities for established industry participants with the infrastructure and expertise necessary to support these requirements. Companies pursuing FDA approval or licensure for products regulated as drugs or biological products may be required to undertake substantial research and development programs, including preclinical studies, clinical trials, and regulatory submissions. Although these activities can require significant capital investment and extended development timelines, successful regulatory authorization may provide opportunities for broader commercialization, greater physician acceptance, approved therapeutic indications, and potential access to third-party reimbursement. The Company believes that its manufacturing capabilities, scientific resources, and relationships with researchers and healthcare professionals may provide a foundation for evaluating participation in such development programs, whether independently or through strategic collaborations.

As part of its long-term strategy, the Company continues to pursue a diversified approach to product development and commercialization designed to capitalize on emerging opportunities while adapting to changes in the regulatory environment. These initiatives include supporting scientific and clinical research, evaluating FDA-authorized development pathways where appropriate, exploring international commercialization opportunities, and expanding its portfolio into product categories and applications governed by different regulatory requirements. The Company’s development initiatives include products incorporating certain proprietary ingredients for topical, aesthetic, and other potential applications, subject to applicable regulatory classifications and requirements. Management believes that the continued diversification of its product portfolio, together with investments in proprietary technologies, strategic scientific collaborations, and advanced manufacturing capabilities, may broaden the Company’s addressable markets and provide additional avenues for future revenue generation.

The Company believes that its integrated operating platform, regulatory diligence, scientific capabilities, and diversified commercialization strategy provide a foundation for pursuing sustainable growth as the regenerative medicine industry evolves. While changes in federal regulatory interpretations, enforcement priorities, or product classifications could affect the Company’s operations or require additional regulatory authorizations, management intends to continue evaluating applicable requirements, strengthening its compliance capabilities, and pursuing opportunities that align with its scientific expertise, manufacturing infrastructure, and long-term business objectives.
Clinical Development as a Competitive Strategy

The Company views clinical research, scientific validation, and the advancement of innovative regenerative medicine technologies as important components of its long-term growth strategy and competitive differentiation. The Company intends to pursue a multifaceted approach to clinical development and commercialization, combining opportunities available under existing regulatory frameworks with the evaluation of FDA-authorized clinical development pathways for selected products and therapeutic applications. Management believes this approach may enable the Company to capitalize on near-term commercial opportunities while building the scientific foundation necessary to support broader market acceptance, product differentiation, and long-term enterprise value creation.

For selected regenerative medicine products and indications, the Company intends to evaluate and, where commercially appropriate, pursue clinical development programs designed to support potential FDA approval or licensure. Successful completion of such programs could provide meaningful competitive advantages, including increased acceptance among physicians, hospitals, and other healthcare institutions; stronger clinical evidence supporting product safety and efficacy; greater differentiation from products that have not received FDA approval; and potential opportunities for coverage and reimbursement through governmental and private third-party payors. The Company believes that its specialized manufacturing infrastructure, analytical capabilities, scientific expertise, and relationships with researchers and healthcare professionals may provide a foundation for pursuing these initiatives independently or through strategic collaborations, licensing arrangements, and other development partnerships.

Concurrently, the Company intends to pursue commercial opportunities for qualifying products under applicable federal and state regulatory frameworks, including opportunities within the private-pay healthcare market. Management believes that this approach may allow the Company to develop its commercial operations and expand physician relationships while evaluating longer-term clinical development opportunities. Where appropriate and legally permissible, the Company also intends to support the collection and evaluation of real-world safety and patient outcome data, which may contribute to scientific understanding, inform future research priorities, and help identify promising applications for further clinical investigation. Such data would not necessarily satisfy the evidentiary requirements for FDA approval or licensure.

The Company believes that integrating scientific research, clinical development, strategic collaborations, and commercialization activities within a coordinated business strategy may provide a competitive advantage as the regenerative medicine industry continues to evolve. By pursuing multiple development and commercialization pathways, the Company seeks to diversify its product portfolio, expand its potential addressable markets, strengthen relationships with healthcare providers and research institutions, and position itself to participate in emerging therapeutic opportunities. Management believes this strategy, supported by the Company’s manufacturing infrastructure and access to scientific resources within Nova Southeastern University’s research environment, provides a foundation for innovation, potential future revenue growth, and long-term shareholder value creation.

The successful development, regulatory authorization, and commercialization of regenerative medicine products remain subject to scientific, clinical, financial, and regulatory uncertainties. There can be no assurance that any clinical development program will result in FDA approval or licensure, that the Company will obtain sufficient resources to complete such programs, or that its commercialization strategies will achieve their intended objectives. In addition, applicable federal and state regulatory requirements may change or be interpreted differently by regulatory authorities, potentially affecting the Company’s ability to develop, manufacture, distribute, or commercialize certain products.
Products and Competitive Landscape

The Company operates within a broad and evolving marketplace encompassing regenerative medicine, cellular and tissue-based technologies, biologics, advanced wound care, orthopedic and sports medicine applications, pain management, and aesthetic products. Management believes that continued advances in biotechnology, increasing scientific interest in regenerative medicine, and growing demand for personalized healthcare, healthy aging, and longevity-related solutions may create meaningful opportunities for companies capable of developing, manufacturing, and commercializing differentiated biological products. The Company’s strategy is to leverage its established manufacturing infrastructure, specialized scientific capabilities, quality management systems, and physician relationships to compete across multiple product categories while progressively expanding its portfolio through proprietary product development, intellectual property licensing, and strategic scientific collaborations.

The regenerative medicine marketplace encompasses a diverse range of allogeneic and autologous products, conventional therapeutic alternatives, and emerging biological technologies. Allogeneic products include materials derived from human perinatal tissues, including placental tissue, amniotic tissue and fluid, umbilical cord tissue, Wharton’s jelly, cord blood, and other human tissue sources. Products within these categories differ substantially in their source materials, manufacturing and processing methodologies, biological composition, intended applications, regulatory classifications, pricing, and supporting scientific evidence. Management believes that product quality and consistency, manufacturing sophistication, biological characterization, analytical testing, and the availability of reliable scientific information are increasingly important factors influencing physician acceptance and competitive differentiation. The Company’s capabilities in cellular processing, extracellular vesicle characterization, microbiological testing, sterility assessment, and other analytical procedures support its strategy of providing products manufactured under established quality management processes.

In addition to its existing product offerings, the Company believes that emerging advances in cellular engineering, extracellular vesicle technologies, biologically active proteins, growth factors, and other regenerative medicine platforms may create opportunities for the development of next-generation biological products. Management is evaluating technologies and potential commercial relationships involving advanced cellular systems, engineered extracellular vesicles, and innovative approaches to the delivery of biologically active substances. These initiatives may include technologies designed to enhance the functional characteristics of cellular products, develop differentiated extracellular vesicle formulations, and support the investigation of new therapeutic applications. The Company intends to pursue such opportunities through internal research and development, licensing arrangements, acquisitions, and collaborations with scientists, academic institutions, and biotechnology companies, as appropriate. Management believes that integrating emerging scientific technologies with the Company’s existing manufacturing and analytical infrastructure may provide a foundation for future product differentiation, intellectual property development, and expansion into additional markets. These technologies remain subject to scientific validation, applicable regulatory requirements, and the successful completion of any necessary development and commercialization activities.

The regenerative medicine marketplace also includes autologous products and procedures involving a patient’s own blood, bone marrow, adipose tissue, and other biological materials. These approaches include platelet-rich plasma, bone marrow-derived preparations, and other physician-administered procedures. Although autologous and allogeneic technologies may address overlapping areas of clinical interest, they differ in their sourcing, processing, manufacturing, distribution, and operational requirements. Management believes that the Company’s allogeneic manufacturing capabilities provide opportunities to offer physicians standardized, premanufactured biological products, where legally permitted, potentially reducing certain logistical complexities associated with patient-specific collection and processing. The regulatory classification of any autologous or allogeneic product depends upon its characteristics, processing, intended use, and other applicable criteria, and autologous status alone does not exempt a product or procedure from FDA regulation.

The Company also views the expanding market for aesthetic, wellness, and topical products as a complementary opportunity for commercial diversification and product innovation. This market includes serums, creams, and other formulations incorporating peptides, proteins, growth factors, and additional biologically derived or bioactive ingredients. Through the development of products incorporating certain proprietary ingredients, the Company intends to pursue opportunities within selected topical and aesthetic product categories. Management believes that these initiatives may enable the Company to leverage its scientific expertise, formulation capabilities, and existing commercial relationships to address additional market segments and broaden its potential customer base. The regulatory requirements applicable to these products vary depending upon their composition, labeling, intended use, and marketing claims, and certain products or claims may require FDA authorization before commercialization.

The Company’s competitive landscape includes biotechnology companies, manufacturers, tissue processors, distributors, healthcare technology providers, and suppliers of conventional therapeutic alternatives. Companies with which the Company has historically competed in certain segments of the regenerative medicine and allogeneic biologics markets include Kimera Labs, Frontier Biologics, Platinum Biologics, Benev Company Inc., Exocel Bio, Re-gen Active Lab, Neobiosis, MiMedx Group, Inc., Invitrx Therapeutics, Signature Biologics, Direct Biologics, and Vitti Labs LLC, together with numerous distributors marketing products manufactured or supplied by third parties. The Company also competes with tissue banks and suppliers of blood, bone, and soft tissue products, companies offering autologous regenerative medicine technologies, and manufacturers of conventional pharmaceutical, wound care, orthopedic, and aesthetic products. These market participants vary significantly in their operating models, financial resources, product portfolios, regulatory status, scientific capabilities, and commercialization strategies. FDA Regulation of Human Cellular and Tissue-Based Products

The FDA regulates human cells, tissues, and cellular and tissue-based products (“HCT/Ps”) under the Public Health Service Act (“PHS Act”), the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (“FD&C Act”), and applicable regulations, including 21 C.F.R. Part 1271.

Certain HCT/Ps that satisfy all applicable criteria under 21 C.F.R. § 1271.10(a) are regulated solely under Section 361 of the PHS Act and generally are not required to obtain FDA premarket approval. These criteria include requirements relating to minimal manipulation, homologous use, combination with other articles, and the role of living-cell metabolic activity in the product’s primary function. Qualifying products remain subject to applicable regulatory requirements, including establishment registration and listing, donor eligibility, current good tissue practices, recordkeeping, and other requirements intended to prevent the introduction, transmission, and spread of communicable diseases.

HCT/Ps that do not qualify for regulation solely under Section 361 may be regulated as drugs, biological products, or medical devices under Section 351 of the PHS Act and/or the FD&C Act. Depending upon their regulatory classification, such products generally require applicable FDA authorization, clearance, or approval before they may be lawfully marketed in the United States.

The regulatory classification of a product depends upon its specific characteristics, processing methods, intended use, labeling, and other relevant factors. The Company recognizes that FDA establishment registration does not constitute FDA approval of any particular product or a determination that a product qualifies for regulation solely under Section 361.

The FDA has undertaken enforcement actions involving certain regenerative medicine products that the agency considers to be marketed without required authorization or otherwise in violation of applicable federal requirements. The FDA’s period of enforcement discretion concerning certain HCT/P premarket approval requirements ended in May 2021, and the agency continues to exercise regulatory oversight of this sector.
